name: Thailand

findings.summary: True selected Ericsson as 5G radio access network vendor for its national 5G network covering northern, central-western and upper southern Thailand on 700 MHz, 2.6 GHz and 26 GHz.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish (third pole). Contract value not disclosed; True has since merged with DTAC, so current RAN vendor split is unverified.

findings.summary: True Move selected ZTE 5G macro base stations and indoor units to build a commercial tri-band 5G network, apparently alongside Ericsson in other regions.
findings.analyst_inference: Geographic split between ZTE and Ericsson inferred from the two separate awards; not stated in one source.

findings.summary: AIS signed memorandums of understanding with Nokia, Huawei and ZTE to develop 5G use cases for industry verticals; no supply contract disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded prc because two of three MOU partners are PRC vendors; the Nokia MOU is third-pole. AIS ran a 5G core tender in July 2020 with Huawei among five bidders; outcome not found.

findings.summary: BOI approved investment promotion for a hyperscale data centre by Google subsidiary Quartz Computing in Chonburi, valued at THB 32.8 billion.
findings.analyst_inference: BOI promotion approval coded tier 2 (approval, not construction). USD value not given per project; not converted.

findings.controller: GDS (Digitalland Services, subsidiary of GDS IDC Services)
findings.summary: BOI approved a THB 28 billion hyperscale data centre in Chonburi by Digitalland Services, described as a GDS IDC Services subsidiary.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: GDS Holdings is PRC-headquartered, but its international business was restructured into a separately financed, Singapore-based entity; which one controls this project is unclear.

findings.local_actor: NextGen Data Center and Cloud Services
findings.summary: BOI approved an 84 MW hyperscale data centre in Navanakorn Industrial Estate, Pathum Thani, by a DAMAC Digital subsidiary, worth THB 26.7 billion.
findings.analyst_inference: DAMAC Digital is Dubai-based (third pole). USD figure is Telecom Review Asia's own conversion.

findings.controller: Unknown (company described as related to DAMAC unit)
findings.local_actor: Zenith Data Center and Cloud Services
findings.summary: BOI approved a 200 MW hyperscale data centre in Navanakorn Industrial Estate, Pathum Thani, by Zenith Data Center and Cloud Services, worth THB 54.9 billion.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: TechNode calls it a related company (apparently of the DAMAC unit) but Telecom Review Asia gives no parent; controller unconfirmed. USD figure is Telecom Review Asia's conversion.

findings.summary: BOI approved a 12 MW data centre in Huai Khwang, Bangkok, by KDDI subsidiary Telehouse Thailand, worth THB 7.55 billion.
findings.analyst_inference: KDDI is Japanese (third pole). USD figure is Telecom Review Asia's conversion.

findings.summary: BOI approved an 80 MW data centre in Amata City Chonburi by ZDATA subsidiary Vistas Technology; reported value THB 9.09 billion or 9.9 billion depending on source.
findings.analyst_inference: PRC pole rests on Telecom Review Asia describing ZDATA Technologies as Chinese; TechNode does not state nationality. Sources disagree on THB value; USD figure is Telecom Review Asia's conversion of THB 9.9bn.

findings.local_actor: Thai government data centre supervision commission / NESDC
findings.reversal_of: construction of 49 data centres under way (tier 4) and approvals for 117 planned facilities
findings.summary: Government suspended construction of 49 data centres and froze approval of 117 planned facilities while it drafts new rules, citing power, water and community impacts.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: affected projects and their controllers were not disclosed, so the pole of what was paused is unknown. Pause is regulatory and resource-driven, not vendor-targeted; Light Reading links it to an oil leak at DAMAC Digital's BKK01 site.

findings.summary: SIAM.AI, Thailand's first Nvidia Cloud Partner, launched an Nvidia H100 GPU cluster for a sovereign cloud, planning H200 and GB200 expansion; Nvidia said it would work with the Thai government.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 4 (deployed) rather than 5 because GPU count, value and utilisation are undisclosed. No S1/S2 source seen, so not corroborated. Taipei Times reports the CEO is reportedly related to Thaksin Shinawatra.

findings.controller: MDES / Big Data Institute / NECTEC consortium
findings.summary: ThaiLLM, a Thai-language foundation model in 8B and 30B versions trained on over 100 billion Thai tokens on the ThaiSC supercomputer, was publicly launched with playground, API and downloads.
findings.analyst_inference: Corroborated set false: GovInsider confirms the programme and developers but predates the launch, so the launch itself rests on one S1 government source. Base model undisclosed; if built on a foreign open-weight model, the update-control pole may differ.

findings.local_actor: Office of the Public Sector Development Commission
findings.summary: SCBX and the public sector development office launched a pilot chatbot on SCBX's Thai-language Typhoon model to guide officials, with plans to extend to other government services.
findings.analyst_inference: SCBX is a Thai financial group, so domestic pole.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
findings.summary: Huawei Cloud and the digital economy ministry signed an MOU on AI development, industry applications, ecosystem building and talent at Huawei Cloud's 2023 Thailand summit.
findings.analyst_inference: Exact signing date not given in the article.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
findings.summary: Report says the ministry partnered with Huawei Cloud, resulting in an e-government cloud launch and support for an Eastern Economic Corridor smart-city project; no terms disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Article reads as vendor publicity, so treated S4 (evidence a claim was made). Tier 3 is provisional: no contract, value or scope disclosed; a human should verify whether a Huawei-hosted e-government cloud is operational.

applications.null_reason: one search on Huawei/Hikvision safe-city and police CCTV returned only Hikvision's own newsroom (uncitable) and paywalled trade pages; no citable procurement found

power.null_reason: no power supply tied specifically to an AI or data-centre project surfaced; power concerns appear only as the stated reason for the 2026 data-centre pause (THA-010)

research_gaps: Outcome of AIS's July 2020 5G core tender (Nokia, Ericsson, Huawei, ZTE, Samsung) and current Huawei share of AIS and NT radio networks.
Current RAN/core vendor mix after the True-DTAC merger.
Which of the 49 paused data centres and 117 frozen approvals belong to which controllers (US, PRC, Gulf, Japanese); whether Google, GDS or ZDATA projects are affected; content of the new rules.
Controller of Zenith Data Center and Cloud Services and whether GDS's Thai project sits with GDS Holdings (PRC) or its spun-out international business.
SIAM.AI GPU count, value and any US export licence; status of the reported July 2025 US plan to require AI-chip licences for Thailand.
ThaiLLM base model and training compute; any government agreement with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft or a PRC model provider (none found).
Scope and status of the Huawei Cloud e-government cloud reported in 2024; safe-city/surveillance procurement (Hikvision, Dahua, Huawei) via S1 procurement records.
